definitions.explanation: The largest figure in a set of measurements or the highest value a function or quantity takes. A technical term used in mathematics, statistics, and engineering.

examples.japanese: グラフの{最大値|さいだいち}を{読|よ}み{取|と}る。
examples.english: Read off the maximum value from the graph.

examples.japanese: {測定|そくてい}した{中|なか}で{最大値|さいだいち}は{五十|ごじゅう}だった。
examples.english: The maximum value among the measurements was fifty.

examples.japanese: {気温|きおん}の{最大値|さいだいち}と{最小値|さいしょうち}の{差|さ}が{大|おお}きいほど、{体調|たいちょう}を{崩|くず}しやすい。
examples.english: The larger the gap between the maximum and minimum temperature values, the easier it is to fall ill.

notes:
{最大|さいだい} (largest) + {値|ち} (value). The {値|ち} reading appears only in technical compounds; the same kanji is read {値|あたい} on its own.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {最大値|さいだいち}を{求|もと}める: to find the maximum value
- {最大値|さいだいち}を{取|と}る: to take its maximum value
- {最大値|さいだいち}を{超|こ}える: to exceed the maximum value

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {最小値|さいしょうち}: minimum value — the direct opposite
- {平均値|へいきんち}: average value — the same {値|ち} pattern applied to the mean
